fomc-2026-09.standing: The rate-setting committee of the US central bank, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds target. Because dollar funding is priced off it worldwide, its decisions reach borrowers far outside the country that elects it.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The committee meets after August consumer prices rose 0.4% and a payroll surge, with oil near $105 following the Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha — an imported supply shock arriving alongside domestic strength. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call Friday. What it settles is whether the Fed treats a war premium as something to look through.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate and vote individually on it. Bank Rate feeds British mortgages, most of which reprice within five years, and the gilt market prices against it.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate and steer long-term yields. It is the anchor for a vast pool of domestic savings that funds borrowing worldwide, and the yen trades on what it signals.
boj-2026-09.recent: The board meets while Tokyo is openly weighing whether to steer pension money as a currency instrument — a route that would defend the yen without touching rates at all. Global bond yields are at multi-decade highs, which makes the gap between Japanese and foreign returns the thing this decision moves, and the question is whether the board treats the yen as its problem or the finance ministry's.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of UK consumer prices, published mid-month for the month before. It sets the benchmark the Bank of England targets, and it mechanically drives rail fares, benefits uprating and index-linked gilt payouts.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The release lands after a stretch in which petrol costs pushed inflation sharply higher elsewhere and oil prices extended gains on Mideast supply fears, putting the fuel component under scrutiny again. Long-dated bond markets have already repriced, with the 10-year Treasury yield reaching 5%, so the September print will settle how much of the pressure is energy passing through and how much is domestic.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's rate-setting body, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds target. It is the anchor rate for the world's reserve currency, so its decisions price credit far beyond the United States.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee meets after a war-driven oil shock turned the question from when to cut to whether to hike: Brent near $110 pushed August consumer prices up 0.4%, and Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call. A payroll surge lifted hike odds further, while the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5% — the market pricing inflation the Fed has not contained.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the interest rate on euro deposits for the twenty countries sharing the currency. It meets roughly every six weeks, and its decisions set the cost of credit from Lisbon to Helsinki.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate and the scale of its bond buying. It anchors the world's cheapest major funding currency, so its decisions travel well beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Tokyo has been weighing whether to steer the yen with pension money — the 2014 playbook — a currency defence run entirely outside the Bank's rate lever. This meeting settles whether the board treats the yen's level as a monetary problem or a fund-flow one, after a yen surge that already pulled the dollar down.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which votes eight times a year on Bank Rate — the rate at which it lends to commercial banks. That rate feeds through to British mortgages, business lending and sterling, making it the main lever over the cost of money in the UK.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee's next vote sets Bank Rate heading into winter, settling what households coming off fixed mortgage deals and firms rolling over debt will pay. There is nothing before this meeting that marks it out from a routine one; what it decides is the borrowing cost the UK carries into the new year.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's rate-setting body, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds target. It is the price of dollars, so its decisions reach every borrower and every currency pegged to or funded in them.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee's last easing argument has collapsed into its opposite: August consumer prices rose 0.4% as a Gulf war reached the price index, oil jumped to $105 after Houthis captured Mocha, and a payroll surge pushed hike odds to two-in-three. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call. What December settles is whether a supply shock the Fed cannot reach has become an inflation it must answer.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of heads of state and government from nineteen countries plus the European and African Unions, hosted by a presidency that rotates each year and sets the agenda. It has no treaty power; what it produces is a communiqué the members have to agree to sign.
g20-2026-miami.recent: This summit lands with the coalition's cohesion itself in question: European finance ministers boycotted the G20 family photo when Siluanov returned, and Trump has welcomed Russia back over EU objections. Zelensky has said he is ready to meet Putin face-to-face in Miami, while Moscow keeps a Putin-Trump-Xi summit open without committing. The guest list is the story.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's rate-setting council, which meets roughly every six weeks to set the deposit rate for the 20 countries sharing the euro. Its decisions price credit for some 350 million people and move the single currency.
ecb-2026-12.recent: An energy shock is doing the arguing for the committee: with Brent near $110 a barrel, the question is whether second-round effects are working through into wages and services, and Deutsche Bank has already raised its ECB peak to 2.75%. What this meeting settles is how far a price the bank cannot reach gets to set the cost of borrowing.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate — the rate that anchors British mortgage costs, business lending and the pound. Every member's vote is published by name.
boe-2026-12.recent: This is the committee's last scheduled decision of the year, and the vote it publishes settles what British households and firms pay to borrow into the new year. The split matters as much as the outcome: how many members break from the majority, and what the minority says it is weighing, is the part that carries past the day itself.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate and the terms of its government bond purchases. It sets the cost of credit in Japan, and the yen moves with its decisions.
boj-2026-12.recent: Tokyo has been weighing whether to steer the yen with pension money rather than policy, a 2014 playbook back in circulation — which leaves the board deciding rates beside a currency tool it does not hold. The yen surged in September as the dollar slid to its weakest since May, so the exchange rate has already moved.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-09-16.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly tally of receipts at US retailers and food services, the first broad read on household spending in a given month. Consumption drives roughly two-thirds of the American economy, so the print moves rate expectations.
